newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt crudes gain with WTI, trade quiet - May 14.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt crudes gain with WTI, trade quiet - May 14.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes gained solely on increases in other domestic grades Wednesday, as local trade remained quiet, players said.
Activity has stayed flat following last week's sale of two cargoes of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude at sharply lower discounts.
ANS traded for $1.50 under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing crude, the U.S. benchmark grade.
In response to lower discounts, BP, the biggest producer of ANS, lowered on Monday its offer to $1.30 under WTI, where it remained Wednesday.
The unchanged discounts and 25-cent rise on WTI lifted outright ANS prices to $19.75/19.95 a barrel.
Kern River crude prices remained flat after Monday's rise in postings, to $14.50/14.60 a barrel.
Line 63 markets remained idle, while ashphalt crude Wilmington rose with postings to $16.35/16.45.
